items.update: With rate limiting disabled in the fake config, the actual HUD handler receives one source-produced spawn payload and schedules one emoji; emoji-rain:clear returns it to the empty state. Any pixel claim still requires a real isolated renderer capture.
items.negative: Return disabled config and verify spawn is ignored. Reject invalid, non-finite, out-of-range or extra-field opacity payloads without changing container opacity. Delay the initial GET response until after a newer opacity event and verify it cannot overwrite that event; on reconnect verify a fresh GET wins over an older outstanding read.
items.cleanup: Send the existing emoji-rain:clear event and close the isolated source; verify the renderer loop/socket stops. No plugin backend, preset, user mapping, or config file may be created.

readGetContracts.contract: Existing GET handler returns only overlayState.opacity; public registry allows GET/HEAD. The HUD reads this on initialization and reconnect and applies it to #canvas-container, with newer socket values taking precedence.

opacityCheck.producer: POST /api/emoji-rain/overlay/opacity updates in-memory state and emits this event.
opacityCheck.expected: The existing socket handler sets #canvas-container.style.opacity to 0.35 for all contained particle layers; diagnostics outside the container remain independent. Default is 1, and 0 hides particles without stopping physics. A visible particle before/after change still requires actual renderer capture and independent image review.
